extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators, environmental compliance staff, and regulators of gasoline distribution facilities (bulk gasoline terminals, cargo tank operators), and stakeholders participating in EPA rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and final rule guidance specifying technology, monitoring, operating, testing, and compliance requirements for gasoline distribution source categories (bulk terminals, cargo tanks, storage vessels, VRUs, loading racks) under NESHAP and NSPS provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Heating Value (NHV) monitoring or initial assessment for air-assisted combustion units
rubrics_metrics.description: Require either continuous monitoring of the net heating value (NHV) of vapors discharged to the flare or thermal oxidation system or perform an initial assessment to determine a minimum gasoline loading rate operating limit that ensures high combustion efficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators may establish a minimum gasoline loading rate operating limit, in addition to or instead of a minimum ratio of gasoline to total product loading rate, to ensure vapor flow rates are high enough for a set air-assist rate to demonstrate compliance with the NHV operating parameter (40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3)(vii)). If the air-assist rate is too high, facilities can lower the air-assist rate or add auxiliary fuel per 40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3)(viii) to ensure sufficient heat release. Without such assessment, a pilot flame and daily inspections are not considered adequate assurance of meeting a 35 mg/L TOC emission limit at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary fuel or air-assist adjustments to ensure combustion efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: If NHV or vapor flow is inadequate for effective combustion at low loading rates, facilities must lower air-assist rates or add auxiliary fuel to ensure high combustion efficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities that cannot meet NHV limits based on minimum gasoline loading rate may determine a minimum auxiliary fuel addition rate (including options like dual-speed or variable-speed blowers) needed to ensure good combustion efficiencies at lower flow rates that may not be represented during high-rate performance tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS requirement for VRU continuous compliance with TOC limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Require continuous monitoring using a CEMS for VRUs to demonstrate compliance with the TOC emission concentration limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CEMS can directly assess compliance with the emission limit; design and operating parameters alone do not provide the same direct assessment. EPA requires CEMS for VRUs across rules, including NESHAP subpart BBBBBB, but provides a limited, short-term alternative for CEMS outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited temporary alternative monitoring during CEMS outages for VRUs
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow a short-term alternative monitoring method to be used during CEMS outages for up to 240 hours in a calendar year (temporary means to demonstrate compliance during periods of CEMS outages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The alternative is based on recent CEMS-derived data (e.g., regeneration cycle times normalized by product loading quantities) and operating parameters used to meet the emission limit when the CEMS was operating. EPA considers 240 hours (about 2 weeks) adequate for maintenance or replacement and emphasizes this is a limited, temporary option—not a substitute for continuous CEMS use. Provisions specify how cycle times and operating limits are established based on operations just prior to the CEMS outage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidation system compliance methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal oxidation systems may either monitor combustion zone temperature or use the flare monitoring alternative to demonstrate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is maintaining provisions that allow monitoring of combustion zone temperature as an acceptable compliance method, or alternatively use the flare monitoring approach (details cross-referenced in respective rule text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balancing applicability threshold (throughput basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require vapor balancing for bulk gasoline plants based on an annual average actual throughput of 4,000 gallons per day or more (revised from a maximum calculated design throughput threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns the applicability threshold with cost-effectiveness analyses and harmonizes provisions across rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum pressure setting for fixed roof storage vessels in vapor balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the minimum pressure setting for fixed roof storage vessels used in vapor balancing to 18 inches of water column (revised from 2.5 psig).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision was made for consistency and to reflect analysis discussed elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure measurement alternative to pressure CPMS for loading racks
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing sources under NESHAP subpart BBBBBB may either install a pressure CPMS or periodically verify appropriate design and operation by measuring system pressure during performance tests or evaluations following 40 CFR 60.503(d) as an alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is finalizing a monitoring alternative (cross-reference to 40 CFR 63.11092(h)) allowing pressure measurements made during performance tests/assessments as an alternative to continuous pressure CPMS to determine the system is at or below 18 inches of water pressure during product loading. This clarifies options for existing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cargo tank vapor-tightness certification levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize a graduated cargo tank vapor tightness certification requirement ranging from 0.50 to 1.25 inches of water pressure drop over a 5-minute period, depending on cargo tank compartment size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This harmonizes requirements across NESHAP subparts R and BBBBBB and NSPS subpart XXa. For NSPS subpart XXa, affected facility tanks must be certified at the lower levels upon startup as required under CAA section 111; if previous contents of a tank are unknown, assume it is a gasoline cargo tank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cargo tank certification compliance schedule (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that all gasoline cargo tanks loaded must be certified at the lower vapor-tightness levels within 3 years of the promulgation date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined that ensuring the entire fleet is certified at the lower level within 3 years meets CAA requirements for expeditious compliance and eliminated additional year-long phase-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit loading to vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks using specified procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading is limited to vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks using the procedures specified in 40 CFR 60.502a(e) (and related test methods in 40 CFR 60.503a(f) and 40 CFR 63.11092(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA revised table entries to reference the correct NSPS subpart XXa requirements and added cross-references to NESHAP test-method sections to ensure annual certification testing and methods are properly cited and enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: External floating roof fitting requirements for storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Require additional fitting requirements for storage vessels with external floating roofs as specified in 40 CFR 60.112b(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined these additional fitting requirements are cost-effective and finalizes them as proposed to reduce emissions from external floating roof vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal floating roof LEL limit (emission limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require internal floating roof storage vessels to maintain concentrations of vapors inside the vessel above the floating roof to less than 25 percent of the lower explosive limit (LEL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated effectively as an emission limitation (not just monitoring). Failure (exceedance) triggers corrective action and repair obligations under referenced sections (e.g., 60.113b(a)(2), 63.1063(d)(2)); repairs must be confirmed effective through re-monitoring and meeting the level within the timeframes in 60.113b(a)(2) or 63.1063(e). EPA relied on NFPA standards and State rules to support the 25% LEL limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL monitoring procedures and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify LEL testing procedures for internal floating roofs, including test duration, calibration, frequency, conditions, and wind limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key procedural provisions: monitoring is required at least once every 12 months (annual); test duration retains a 20-minute period but allows discontinuing testing when one 5-minute average exceeds 25% LEL; calibration may use other gases with appropriate correction factors but calibration should be made with tubing attached; tests should be conducted when the internal floating roof is floating with limited product movement; LEL measurements shall be taken when wind speed at the top of the tank is 5 mph or less to the extent practicable, but not when sustained wind speed at top of tank is greater than the annual average wind speed at the site or 15 mph, whichever is less; re-monitoring is required to confirm repairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed roof storage vessel pressure relief opening pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Set minimum pressure relief device opening pressure for fixed roof storage vessels to 18 inches of water (0.65 psig).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revises the previously proposed 2.5 psig minimum to 18 inches water column for consistency across provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual instrument monitoring for equipment leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Require semiannual instrument monitoring of all equipment in gasoline service using either optical gas imaging (OGI) according to proposed appendix K to 40 CFR part 60 (appendix K) or EPA Method 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities must repair any leaks identified from an instrument monitoring event or any leaks identified by audible/visual/olfactory (AVO) methods during normal duties. Commenters raised concerns that EPA cost estimates for instrument monitoring may be understated; EPA retained the semiannual instrument monitoring requirement as proposed.
